newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares seen rising more after volatile day.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares seen rising more after volatile day.

text.p: Danish share prices closed higher on Tuesday after a volatile day of fluctuation with renewed investor interest seen triggering more rises again on Wednesday.

"The market started off positively enough but a dearth of buyers pulled the index down around noon. In the afternoon things bucked up, investors began showing renewed interest. We could see further gains now tomorrow," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 0.21 point higher at 154.60. The KFX March future rose 1.45 point to 154.65 with 1,129 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Interest centred a good deal on Novo Nordisk and Danisco, which rose eight and five crowns respectively to close at 382 and 616, helping the index on its way back up.
Unidanmark was the only one of the top banks to decline, ending three crowns lower at 349. Superfos shed 6.7 crowns to 790 two days before its 1996 result is to be announced.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.121 billion crowns.
